2.text: CHARMS OF THE MARITIME CHUKCHEE. — On the whole, the charms of

3.text: the Maritime Chukchee are quite similar to those of the Reindeer people.

4.text: The differences discoverable are largely due to differences in their mode of life.

5.text: Family Charms. — In olden times, both the Maritime Chukchee and the

6.text: Eskimo used the wooden fire-drill; but at present it is never used, even for

7.text: ceremonial purposes. Nevertheless, the Maritime Chukchee guard against an

8.text: interchange of fire, although the observance of this interdiction is more lax with

9.text: them than it is among the Reindeer people, and in recent years it is neglected

10.text: to a considerable degree. The bringing into the house of utensils or sacred

11.text: images belonging to an “alien” house is likewise forbidden, as I had occasion

12.text: to notice while making the collections for the Museum. Even while travelling

13.text: in a skin boat it is reprehensible to take fire from an “alien” hearth, or to

14.text: borrow kettles, because of the soot that covers them. So great is the value

15.text: of skins and timber (the materials for house-building) among the Maritime

16.text: people, in consequence of their scarcity, that a house the owner of which has

17.text: died, leaving no direct heirs, is not left untouched, as is the case with the

18.text: Reindeer people. Some distant relatives will surely come, tear down the house,

19.text: and divide the spoils; but they will be careful not to set foot within the house

21.text: Many of the Maritime Chukchee also have the charm-strings (Fig. 255),

22.text: but they do not attach the importance to them that the reindeer-breeders do.

23.text: The images of their charm-strings, on the whole, are similar to those of the

24.text: reindeer-breeders; but they are intended to help their owners in hunting-pursuits,

25.text: not to protect their herds. These images are usually human figures roughly

26.text: cut out of wood or curried leather, and similar to those previously described.

27.text: Many of the charm-strings also have figures of dogs attached to them, which
